question: Can an off-the-shelf language model forecast continuous time series without parameter updates by serializing values as text, while still yielding useful probabilistic densities and zero-shot behavior across domains?

key_findings.claim: LLMTime turns numerical forecasting into constrained next-token prediction through digit-aware serialization, per-series affine scaling, and sampling from a frozen GPT-3 or LLaMA-2 model.
key_findings.evidence: The encoding removes decimal points at fixed precision, separates digits for GPT tokenizers, separates observations with commas, and reverses a percentile-based scale after generation. Twenty samples provide pointwise medians and quantiles; token log probabilities provide sequence likelihoods.

anchors.section: Appendix A.1-A.2, scaling and validation tuning

key_findings.claim: A digit autoregressive distribution can be interpreted as a high-resolution continuous density by assigning uniform density within each fixed-precision bin and applying the scale change-of-variables term.
key_findings.evidence: For base B and n fractional digits, each text outcome identifies a bin of width B^-n; the reported density adds n log B to the token-string log probability and then adds the log-Jacobian of preprocessing. A 200-sample toy study reports competitive Wasserstein distance on asymmetric, multimodal, and heavy-tailed one-dimensional distributions.

key_findings.claim: On the paper's selected Darts, Monash, and Informer evaluations, frozen LLM forecasts are reported as best or second-best in aggregated MAE, and on Darts they outperform the tested trained baselines in aggregate probabilistic metrics.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 4 aggregates deterministic MAE from pointwise medians; Figure 5 and Appendix Figure 10 report Darts NLL and CRPS against ARIMA, spectral-mixture GP, TCN, N-BEATS, N-HiTS, and PromptCast. Informer covariates are forecast independently, GPT-3 Informer evaluation is skipped for cost, and Monash uses only a tractable subset.

key_findings.claim: The paper attributes useful zero-shot extrapolation to language-model preferences for simple and repetitive continuations, but its own synthetic evidence shows failures on composition, exponential growth, and the distinction between high likelihood and typical samples.
key_findings.evidence: GPT-3 likelihood favors symbolic-regression expressions balancing fit and complexity and extrapolates several primitive patterns; Linear+Cosine is much less reliable in samples, while GPT-4 improves some deterministic compositions but is erratic and worse calibrated on stochastic Darts series.

anchors.section: 5, Origins of Zero-Shot Performance and Figure 6

key_findings.claim: Text-native inputs enable missing-value markers and limited natural-language reasoning, but these demonstrations are narrow and expose disconnects between numerical continuation and verbal explanation.
key_findings.evidence: LLaMA-2 70B accepts literal NaN tokens and remains competitive in CRPS with baselines that receive linearly interpolated data. In an 11-way synthetic-function identification task, GPT-4 improves with chain-of-thought, yet three classes have zero accuracy and the appendix includes confident, factually wrong explanations.

anchors.section: 6, Connecting time series and textual understanding

key_findings.claim: The likelihood appendix contains an invalid intermediate algebraic equality, although its final renormalization expression and released implementation use the correct adjustment.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix A.3 prints 1/tilde(p)=exp(l0)+1/p and then tilde(p)=(1/p-exp(l0))^-1; neither follows from tilde(p)=p/(1-exp(l0)). The final line log tilde(p)=log p-log(1-exp(l0)) is correct. Artifact commit f74234c implements adjusted_logprobs = logprobs - log(1-p_extra), with p_extra approximated only from disallowed tokens among the API's top-five log probabilities.

anchors.section: Appendix A.3, Equations for likelihood adjustment

key_findings.claim: Two additional source/artifact inconsistencies prevent treating the headline aggregates as mechanically exact.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 4 says the three benchmarks collectively contain 29 datasets, while the described components are 8 Darts, 19 Monash, and 5 Informer datasets; the Appendix says 19 Monash datasets but lists only 18. Separately, the paper's precision-2 example maps 1.23 to digit string 123, while the released serializer's repeated floating subtraction and integer casts map 1.23 to 122 and deserialize it as 1.22 in a focused smoke test.

method.core_idea: Reuse a frozen causal language model as a zero-shot probabilistic forecaster by representing each rescaled real-valued observation as a controlled sequence of digit tokens.
method.mechanism: For each series, shift and scale using training-history quantiles; quantize to fixed decimal precision; serialize digits and time separators in a tokenizer-specific format; constrain or bias generation toward legal numeric tokens; draw multiple continuations; deserialize and invert the scale; and estimate MAE, CRPS, or continuous NLL. Hyperparameters are selected by likelihood on a held-out suffix without updating LLM weights.
assumptions: The frozen model has learned sequence-completion biases that transfer from text/code pretraining to numeric patterns.
The chosen tokenizer exposes a stable digit-level representation or can be forced toward one with spaces and logit bias.
Quantization at two or three decimal places preserves the forecast-relevant signal.
A per-series affine scale derived from the observed history remains suitable over the forecast horizon.
Sampling and token likelihood behavior of proprietary or externally hosted base models is stable enough for comparison.
For multivariate Informer data, forecasting each covariate independently is an adequate reduction.
The top-five disallowed-token mass is an adequate approximation to total invalid-token mass for GPT likelihood renormalization.
Selected benchmark subsets and validation-likelihood tuning yield representative comparisons despite compute and context constraints.

techniques.role: Aligns numerical strings with the base model's tokenizer and removes redundant decimal points.
Controls digit length while retaining some examples that cross an order-of-magnitude boundary.
Uses logit bias, temperature, and nucleus sampling to favor parseable numeric continuations.
Builds medians, quantiles, and empirical CRPS from repeated text completions.
Converts fixed-precision token probabilities into piecewise-uniform continuous densities.
Tunes scaling, precision, temperature, and baseline hyperparameters on a pseudo-forecast suffix.
Tests three series recorded after the stated GPT-3 training cutoff.
Compares GPT likelihoods across symbolic-regression candidates of different fit and complexity.

evaluations.setting: Eight univariate Darts series with the final 20 percent held out
evaluations.metric: MAE from 20-sample medians, empirical CRPS, and continuous NLL per dimension
evaluations.result: GPT-3 and LLaMA-2 70B are reported competitive in MAE and best in aggregate CRPS/NLL among the tested methods, with pronounced gains on short, seasonal series and less consistent behavior on long/noisy series.
evaluations.baseline: ARIMA, spectral-mixture GP, TCN, N-BEATS, N-HiTS, and PromptCast

evaluations.setting: Compute-filtered subset of the Monash archive
evaluations.metric: MAE normalized per dataset before aggregation
evaluations.result: GPT-3/LLaMA-2 are reported among the top aggregate ranks, but individual rows include substantial losses and the paper's claimed count, listed count, artifact files, and 29-dataset headline do not reconcile.
evaluations.baseline: SES, Theta, TBATS, ETS, ARIMA, pooled regression, CatBoost, FFNN, DeepAR, N-BEATS, WaveNet, Transformer, and last value

evaluations.setting: Five multivariate Informer-family datasets at horizons 96 and 192, each channel forecast independently
evaluations.result: LLaMA-2 70B is competitive in aggregate at both horizons but ranges from best to worst across datasets and loses relative ground at horizon 192, especially on electricity and traffic.
evaluations.baseline: Informer, Reformer, Transformer, Autoformer, and FEDformer

evaluations.setting: Synthetic primitive and compositional sequences with 140 context steps
evaluations.metric: Forecast samples, NLL, and symbolic-expression likelihood
evaluations.result: Primitive linear, periodic, and several multiplicative patterns are extrapolated well; exponential and additive-compositional patterns are unreliable, and likelihood quality can exceed sample quality.
evaluations.baseline: ARIMA and TCN, plus symbolic-regression candidates of increasing complexity

evaluations.setting: Three short series whose observations postdate the stated September 2021 GPT-3 cutoff
evaluations.result: GPT-3 is reported competitive with or better than the fitted baselines on Istanbul traffic, 2022 TSMC stock, and 2022 Turkey power, weakening but not eliminating training-data leakage concerns.
evaluations.baseline: Spectral-mixture GP, TCN, N-HiTS, N-BEATS, and ARIMA

evaluations.setting: Darts series corrupted with random missing observations
evaluations.metric: NLL and CRPS over corruption rate with three random seeds
evaluations.result: Literal NaN serialization is more resilient in NLL and competitive in CRPS with interpolation-based fitted models.
evaluations.baseline: Time-series models fitted after linear interpolation

evaluations.setting: Eleven-way GPT-4 classification of synthetic generating functions over 20 trials per class
evaluations.metric: Accuracy with direct prompting and chain-of-thought
evaluations.result: Chain-of-thought helps on several functions, but x_times_sine, beat, and sinc are always misclassified and appendix examples show incorrect verbal deductions.
evaluations.baseline: Random chance and direct non-chain-of-thought prompting

limitations: The strongest evaluations use historical GPT-3 and GPT-4 APIs or externally hosted LLaMA-2 weights; exact model snapshots, serving kernels, and training corpora are unavailable.

The repository pins OpenAI 0.28.1 but otherwise installs many dependencies without versions, provides no tagged release or automated test suite, and relies on external downloads, API keys, GPUs, and large precomputed archives.
The artifact's decimal conversion truncates rather than robustly rounds and can shift a nominal fixed-precision value by one bin because of floating-point subtraction.
GPT likelihood renormalization observes only the top five token alternatives, so unobserved invalid-token mass remains in the denominator and NLL is approximate.
The continuous-density construction is piecewise uniform within arbitrary quantization bins and its reported NLL is sensitive to precision, separators, scale, tokenizer, and Jacobian bookkeeping.
Monash is filtered for tractability, Informer channels are treated independently, GPT-3 Informer runs are omitted, and the benchmark counts are internally inconsistent.
Training-data leakage cannot be excluded for common public time series; three post-cutoff examples test a narrow alternative but not benchmark contamination or related-pattern exposure.
The RLHF explanation for GPT-4/chat-model degradation is correlational: tokenizer, prompting, API constraints, base architecture, and unavailable likelihoods change simultaneously.
The verbal-understanding study has only 20 trials per function, fixed synthetic generators, incomplete class results in the plot, and no comparison to specialized classifiers.
Context-window cost grows with digits, precision, observations, and variables; only a few hundred observations fit in the evaluated legacy contexts.
failure_modes: Noise perturbs a compressible pattern enough that the LLM's learned sequence prior selects a simple but wrong continuation.
A tokenizer groups digits or inserts nuisance tokens, destroying the regular local structure the method expects.
The series changes scale, sign regime, frequency, or distribution beyond the history-derived affine transform.
Long histories or multivariate inputs exceed context limits, forcing truncation or independent-channel forecasts that discard dependencies.
Composite rules require several arithmetic and copying operations within one autoregressive trajectory and generation drifts despite assigning good likelihood to the truth.
Chat alignment favors explanatory prose or narrow, overconfident completions instead of calibrated numeric samples.
Completion parsing ends early or emits illegal text; the artifact may pad a short forecast with its final parsed value unless strict handling is enabled.
Quantization, floating-point truncation, or a scale Jacobian error changes NLL rankings without changing substantive forecast quality.
A public benchmark or close transformation was present in pretraining, inflating apparent zero-shot generalization.
reusable_insights: Treat numerical representation, scaling, and tokenizer behavior as model components and ablate them independently.
For a discrete autoregressive forecaster, separate sample quality, calibrated probability, and parse success; strong likelihood need not imply typical good generations.
Quantized-token likelihoods can yield continuous densities, but every bin-width and change-of-variables term should be tested with normalized toy distributions.
Evaluate foundation forecasters on temporally held-out and explicitly decontaminated datasets with strong naive/statistical baselines.
Report results by dataset and horizon rather than relying on one normalized aggregate that can hide severe failures.
Preserve textual missingness indicators when missingness itself may be predictive, and compare against learned as well as fixed imputation.
A small frozen model can be useful as a source of priors even when direct zero-shot performance is fragile; representation transfer and task adaptation are separate questions.
Reproducibility checks should round-trip every serializer boundary value and verify token constraints against the exact deployed tokenizer.
open_questions: Does the original LLMTime comparison survive modern leakage-controlled suites such as GIFT-Eval under current foundation-model baselines?
How much of the result comes from language/code pretraining rather than generic autoregressive architecture, synthetic numeric exposure, or benchmark contamination?
Can constrained decoding compute an exact normalized distribution over valid numeric strings without the top-five approximation?
Would robust decimal arithmetic or integer quantization change the reported NLL/CRPS rankings?
Can textual covariates and multivariate dependencies be incorporated without consuming prohibitive context or losing calibration?
Which alignment interventions specifically damage numeric forecasting after controlling tokenizer, model family, prompts, and inference API?
When should a general LLM be preferred to a smaller time-series-pretrained foundation model on accuracy, calibration, latency, energy, and data-governance grounds?

competitive_landscape.title: PromptCast: A New Prompt-based Learning Paradigm for Time Series Forecasting
competitive_landscape.difference: PromptCast expresses history and horizon as a natural-language question and fine-tunes or prompts language models; LLMTime removes task prose, engineers digit tokenization/scaling, and evaluates probabilistic densities.

competitive_landscape.title: One Fits All:Power General Time Series Analysis by Pretrained LM
competitive_landscape.difference: One Fits All adapts a largely frozen pretrained language model with time-series inputs for multiple tasks and trains task components; LLMTime changes no parameters and uses literal numeric text completion.

competitive_landscape.title: Time-LLM: Time Series Forecasting by Reprogramming Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Time-LLM learns a reprogramming and prompt-prefix bridge into a frozen LLM and targets point forecasting; LLMTime is parameter-free and derives probabilistic samples/densities from digit tokens.

competitive_landscape.title: Lag-Llama: Towards Foundation Models for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
competitive_landscape.difference: Lag-Llama pretrains a decoder directly on large time-series collections and produces parametric probabilistic forecasts; LLMTime reuses text pretraining with no time-series training but pays a tokenization and context penalty.

competitive_landscape.title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting
competitive_landscape.difference: TimesFM pretrains a patched continuous time-series decoder for efficient zero-shot point forecasts and covariates; LLMTime uses an existing text LLM and exposes sample-based uncertainty without domain pretraining.

competitive_landscape.title: Unified Training of Universal Time Series Forecasting Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Moirai trains across heterogeneous time-series frequencies with multi-patch inputs and mixture-distribution outputs; LLMTime avoids time-series pretraining but cannot natively share multivariate information.

competitive_landscape.title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
competitive_landscape.difference: Chronos keeps quantized token forecasting but pretrains T5-family models on large real and synthetic time-series corpora with a fixed vocabulary, trading LLMTime's text-only reuse for stronger domain specialization and smaller inference models.

competitive_landscape.title: GIFT-Eval: A Benchmark For General Time Series Forecasting Model Evaluation
competitive_landscape.difference: GIFT-Eval supplies diverse zero-shot datasets, explicit non-leaking pretraining data, and broad statistical/deep/foundation baselines; it is a materially stronger evaluation setting than LLMTime's filtered legacy aggregates.

competitive_landscape.title: Revisiting LLMs as Zero-Shot Time-Series Forecasters: Small Noise Can Break Large Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct adverse replication and robustness critique
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. report that prompt-only LLM forecasters are highly noise-sensitive and often lose to simple domain models, directly narrowing LLMTime's broad zero-shot claim and recommending time-series fine-tuning.

competitive_landscape.title: Sundial: A Family of Highly Capable Time Series Foundation Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Sundial pretrains continuous patch tokens with flow matching on a trillion-point corpus, avoiding LLMTime's discrete bins while retaining sample-based probabilistic forecasts and much shorter sequences.

competitive_landscape.title: TiRex: Zero-Shot Forecasting Across Long and Short Horizons with Enhanced In-Context Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: TiRex pretrains an xLSTM-based time-series model with context masking and reports stronger GIFT-Eval/Chronos-ZS long- and short-horizon results than larger transformer TSFMs; it targets state tracking rather than text-model priors.

competitive_landscape.title: Chronos-2: From Univariate to Universal Forecasting
competitive_landscape.difference: Chronos-2 uses group attention and synthetic relational training for zero-shot univariate, multivariate, and covariate-informed forecasting; it directly addresses LLMTime's independent-channel and side-information limitations.

competitive_landscape.title: Moirai 2.0: When Less Is More for Time Series Forecasting
competitive_landscape.difference: Moirai 2.0 trains a small decoder-only model on 36 million series using multi-token quantile prediction, reporting better speed and accuracy than its larger predecessor; unlike LLMTime, its prior is explicitly time-series-native.

competitive_landscape.title: Reverso: Efficient Time Series Foundation Models for Zero-shot Forecasting
competitive_landscape.difference: Reverso combines long convolutions and DeltaNet layers in models reported over one hundred times smaller than large transformer forecasters while matching them; it weakens the case for paying general-LLM scale costs solely to obtain zero-shot forecasts.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper presents an entirely zero-shot route from off-the-shelf text LLMs to continuous probabilistic time-series forecasts, enabled by digit tokenization, scaling, and a discrete-to-continuous likelihood construction.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Relative to PromptCast and pretrained-LM adaptation work available in 2023, the absence of parameter updates, direct digit continuation, and explicit continuous-density interpretation are distinctive; the paper also probes missingness, scaling, alignment, simplicity bias, and verbal explanations.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The representation-level idea was genuinely catalytic and anticipates tokenized time-series foundation models such as Chronos. Its empirical leadership is now historical: stronger leakage-aware benchmarks, direct noise-sensitive replications, and efficient domain-pretrained models substantially narrow the claim that a general text LLM is an accurate or economical universal forecaster. The algebra, serializer, and dataset-count inconsistencies further require treating exact likelihood and aggregate rankings as artifact-bounded rather than theorem-like facts.
